text.p: Copper prices retreated in London and New York on Friday while CBOT wheat and NYMEX oil traded higher. The CRB Index closed 2.03 points higher at 243.78.

London Metal Exchange copper and aluminium ended near their lows on Friday after upside bids failed to catch fire in a thin market focused on next week's third Wednesday pricing. March COMEX copper settled 0.40 cent weaker at 99.30 cents per pound, traded 100.20 to 98.50 cents. Spot December went out 0.10 cent lower at 102.50 cents. Three-month LME copper finished the evening kerb on the London Metal Exchange (LME) at $2,132, off $26 from Thursday. Nearby spreads were the market's primary focus and remained tight. Heavy business was done in "tomorrow/next day" which traded close to the LME's $23 backwardation limit at $22.50. Cash to threes backwardation continued to narrow, which is exp

Aluminium closely shadowed copper's movements, gaining strength early in the day from an LME stocks drawdown of 2,525 tonnes. But producer forward selling capped the market and it failed to stay above the $1,540 resistance level for any length of time. It ended at its nearby support level of $1,510, down $18. Lead was last bid at $696, down $4 from Thursday's bullish close at the psychological $700 level. Nickel shed $70 to finish at $6,635, under pressure from a sizable 876-tonne increase in stocks. Zinc ended the kerb slightly weaker at $1,053, down $5.

COMEX February gold ended down 40 cents at $370.40, after trading in a narrow $371.90-370.20 range on estimated total volume of 15,000 lots. Spot gold in the bullion market ended quoted $368.45/368.95, down from the London afternoon fix at $369.00, and the New York close Thursday at $368.90/369.40.

CBOT wheat futures closed higher, led by deferred months, on news India was importing rather than exporting wheat, traders said. But some traders said further news overnight that India bought wheat from Australia rather than the U.S. was bearish for nearby December. There was news this week that India would be importing two million tonnes of wheat and overnight there was confirmation that Australia sold one million tonnes to India. Wheat also found support from news the European Union may curb wheat exports next week, traders said. "Next week we may give less. We may turn the screw on exports," said the European Commission's director general Guy Legras. Wheat closed 3/4 to four cents per

A combination of options expiry and a forecast for cold weather in the eastern U.S. lifted NYMEX crude and product futures, but analysts generally saw the market still in weak mode. January crude futures gained 72 cents on the day to settle at $24.44 a barrel, making up about half the losses posted early in the week. Heating oil led the way, rising 3.04 cents to 71.71 cents a gallon, mainly on the weather report.

CSCE world sugar prices ended broadly higher Friday after a sudden burst of short covering late in the session, trading sources said. The key March 1997 contract shot up 0.29 cent at the highs, topping out at 10.75 cents before retracing to 10.73 at the close, its highest in nearly three weeks.
